newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps slip, CFDs and naphtha turn lower.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps slip, CFDs and naphtha turn lower.

text.p: European oil swaps slipped lower on Thursday as Brent crude and naphtha, which had bucked the weaker tone on Wednesday, succumbed to downward pressure.
Brent CFDs slipped a couple of cents a barrel for next week's dates to talk 13 cents under September while the following three weeks slipped about seven to 10 cents a barrel.
Dealers said that oil products continued to weigh heavily on the market.
Gas oil crack spreads against Brent were heard traded at $4.25 a barrel for 4Q97 compared to $4.30 and $4.35 on Wednesday.
Gasoline swaps slipped $1.50 a tonne trading at $185.75 for August before slipping to trade $184.25 on July by late morning.
Brokers pegged July at $184, August $185.00 September at $183,25.
Naphtha also eased $1 a tonne to around $179.50 for August and $180.50 for September.
Heavy fuel swaps were little changed from Thursday as support from the U.S. and Singapore was offset by falling Brent futures.
Rotterdam barges edged up to $86 on the physical market but July swaps stayed around $95 with August 50 cents higher.
Forward levels were little changed with the fourth and first quarters at $92.50 and $95.50 respectively.
Low sulphur also held steady at $92.50 for July but rose to $99.00 for the fourth quarter and $101.50 for the first quarter next year.
